purpose: User-authorized cumulative model correction using tightened T1, Q2 run02 and newly acquired Q2 run03. All three now calibration data. Preserve the frozen-R79 failure on run03; no retrospective validation claim.
comparison: First refit the existing nine parameters on all three. Then test one targeted model extension: separate static breakaway and kinetic friction, with two nonnegative static-minus-kinetic increments. This is a modeling hypothesis, not an identified physical cause.
seedMeaning: Declared numerical starting hypotheses; not measured friction. Three bounded starts for a nonsmooth friction model, all reported. No per-record parameter vectors.
objective: Same normalized full-record waveform plus task-statistic calibration loss as R79, now equal-weighted over all three complete motion/holding snapshots. All native observed samples used:400/400/399. No absent native point imputed. Select lowest full cumulative calibration objective among declared candidates; report every record's before/after metrics and waveform errors.
stictionRule: Use only simulated velocity, with fixed 1e-12 m/s numerical-zero tolerance. At rest OR when a kinetic-only trial crosses zero within the step, allow static reaction up to kinetic+extra and prefer feasible sticking. Otherwise use kinetic friction. This is an event-capture approximation, not phase-specific freezing or measured-velocity feedback. Numerical prototype omitting within-step capture retained separately.
inputLimitations: Moving inputs 1ms recorded queued commands; hold inputs 40-step means, not recovered 1ms waveforms. Command-to-delivered-torque mapping uncalibrated.
recordingLimitations: Run03 has one missing phase3 native CSV frame and 7.08s completion tail; its 8000 moving and300hold records have CRC verified four-copy recovery. T1 tail6.88s. These limitations are retained, not recast as full-protocol-qualified captures.
candidateMeaning: Training-calibrated offline input-replay model, not a validated autonomous plant or evidence of CA versus BLNN superiority.
